description: A simple training app that helps new astronauts learn space mission basics step by step. Trainees practice pre-launch checklists, spacecraft controls, spacewalk safety, and emergency drills in guided simulations. Short lessons cover gravity, orbits, and life in space, while quizzes track progress. A virtual instructor gives hints and feedback, and trainees earn badges as they advance from Recruit to Mission Specialist.
summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer – Command Your Own Space Outpost is an interactive 30-day lunar and Martian base-management simulation built with React, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and a custom JavaScript life-support engine.

Designed for students aged 10–17, it addresses the challenge of teaching complex aerospace engineering without passive textbooks. Players step into the role of Mission Commander, managing eight interconnected survival metrics—oxygen, water, food, energy, radiation shielding, temperature, crew health, and research—while constructing nine outpost facilities, unlocking seven technologies, and navigating random space events and critical dilemmas. An AI Mission Advisor, live telemetry charts, Mission Radio alerts, and contextual engineering explanations connect every gameplay choice to real NASA systems like closed-loop water recycling and radiation shielding.

This matters because future Moon and Mars missions depend on systems thinking and resource trade-offs, not isolated facts. By letting students experience how every watt, liter, and decision directly impacts crew survival, the game turns abstract STEM principles into memorable, hands-on problem-solving and inspires the next generation of space explorers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer – Command Your Own Space Outpost is a 10-screen, turn-based 30-day space survival and engineering simulation. Players configure a Commander profile, choose a difficulty (Easy, Normal, or Expert), and select either the Moon (Lunar Research Outpost) or Mars (Martian Exploration Base)—each with distinct gravity, solar efficiency, temperature swings, and hazard profiles.

On each mission day, a centralized JavaScript simulation engine calculates crew consumption, water recycling recovery, greenhouse food/oxygen output, solar and backup power balance, habitat temperature drift, and radiation shielding across eight live indicators (Oxygen, Water, Food, Energy, Radiation Shielding, Temperature, Crew Health, and Research Points). Players construct and upgrade nine facilities, unlock seven technologies, and respond to eight random space events, five decision challenges, and engineering quizzes before receiving a final Mission Report and Commander Rank on Day 30.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Active STEM Learning: Students aged 10–17 experience engineering trade-offs firsthand—seeing how building a Research Lab or Greenhouse increases energy and water demand—rather than memorizing static facts.
  • Real-World Space Literacy: Every facility and crisis includes an Educational Mode breakdown linking gameplay to real NASA systems (ISS ECLSS water recycling, Mars MOXIE, Kilopower, and Whipple micrometeorite shields).
  • Critical Thinking Under Pressure: The game encourages systems thinking, long-term planning, and calm emergency response, aiming to spark lasting interest in aerospace engineering and STEM careers.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Core Stack: JavaScript (ES6+), React.js, and Tailwind CSS for a responsive, component-driven UI.
  • Data Visualization & Icons: Recharts (real-time resource telemetry area charts and mission performance bar charts) and Lucide React.
  • Browser APIs: Web Audio API (synthesized UI and alert sound effects with mute control), Web Speech API (speechSynthesis for spoken Mission Radio alerts), and localStorage (automatic mission save/resume, Best Mission Score, and Local Leaderboard).

What Makes It Creative

  • AI Mission Advisor: A rule-based diagnostic engine that calculates resource runway in real time and warns players before critical shortages (e.g., "Your water supply may run out in 3 days. Upgrade the Water Recycling Unit.").
  • Immersive Mission Control HUD: Combines custom Lunar and Martian outpost illustrations, an animated starfield, clickable habitat module inspectors, Mission Radio voice alerts, and six unlockable achievement badges.
  • Consequence-Driven Storytelling: Decisions during solar storms, dust storms, or CO₂ spikes immediately reshape resource trajectories and teach the underlying physics principle right after the choice.

Key Factors Considered

  • Game Balance & Realism: Formulas are tuned so success is achievable but not guaranteed, with non-negative resource clamping, early warning thresholds, and a clear label noting that values are simplified educational estimates.
  • Accessibility & UX: High-contrast dark-mode HUD, confirmation dialogs for costly facility builds, synthesized audio with a mute toggle, and responsive layouts for desktop, tablet, and mobile screens.
  • Zero-Backend Portability: Storing saves and local leaderboard scores in localStorage ensures the app works anywhere in a browser without requiring an external server.
